title: Live vs. extract
summary: Switch between a live connection and an extract, change the source, take it offline, set extract filters, aggregation and refresh kinds, and see which file holds what.
intro: A tiny invented table of 16 sessions stands in for a database (it is not the Driftlight data). Switch the connection, press "Add 4 rows, correct 1" to change the source, take it offline, and set the extract's filter, aggregation and refresh kind. The times are made-up numbers that only show how the pieces relate, never real performance. At the bottom, pick a file type to see what it holds.

copy.tableNote: Columns show the view on each connection; the highlighted one is the connection in use. "–" means that member has no rows on that connection.
copy.liveWhat: A live connection sends every query to the original data, so the view always shows what the source holds right now. Nothing is copied.
copy.extractWhat: An extract is a copy of the data, saved separately from the original in a `.hyper` file. Queries run against that copy, not against the source.
copy.liveOffline: A live connection needs the source to be reachable. With the source offline, the view has nothing to query.
copy.extractOffline: Extracts allow offline access: the view keeps working from the copy while the source is unreachable (you just can't refresh).
copy.liveFresh: The live view already includes the new rows and the correction: every query reads the source as it is now.
copy.extractStale: The extract is a snapshot: it changes only when you refresh it, so the source's new rows and corrections are not in the view yet.
copy.extractCurrent: The extract matches the source for the rows it is set to hold, because it was refreshed or the change fell outside its filter.
copy.filterNote: An extract filter keeps only the rows you need; the 2024 rows are not in the extract at all, not just hidden.
copy.aggregateNote: Aggregating for visible dimensions stores pre-aggregated rows instead of every record, so the extract holds one row per Year and Plan.
copy.incrementalBlocked: You can't use incremental refresh together with aggregation, so only a full refresh is available.
copy.fullRefresh: A full refresh replaces all the data in the extract with the latest information from the original data source. It is the default.
copy.incrementalNew: An incremental refresh only includes new rows since the previous refresh, found with a column you choose (here the row id).
copy.incrementalMissed: An incremental refresh adds the new rows but does not pick up changes to rows already in the extract: the corrected row still shows its old value. A full refresh would fix it.
copy.timing: Times here are illustrative: a made-up fixed cost plus a made-up cost per row read.
copy.timingLive: With a live connection the speed depends on the source system, so it is slow when the source is busy and quick when it is fast.
copy.timingExtract: Views on extracts usually perform better than views connected directly to the original data, and queries don't load the database.
copy.filesIntro: Pick a file type and where the data comes from, and see what the file holds. The connection chosen above decides whether an extract exists.
copy.fileTwb: A `.twb` workbook holds worksheets, dashboards and stories, but no data.
copy.fileTwbx: A `.twbx` packaged workbook is a single zip file with the workbook plus any supporting local file data and background images.
copy.fileTds: A `.tds` data source file holds the connection information and metadata such as groups, sets, calculated fields, bins and default properties, but not the actual data. You create it with Add to Saved Data Sources.
copy.fileTdsx: A `.tdsx` packaged data source holds everything a `.tds` does, plus a copy of any local file-based data or extracts.
copy.fileHyper: A `.hyper` file is the extract: the extracted data itself. A live connection has none.
copy.packagedFile: Local file data is packaged into the file.
copy.packagedServerLive: Data from a server isn't packaged unless you extract it first, so with a live connection to a server the file has no data.
copy.packagedServerExtract: The data from a server is extracted, and extracts are packaged, so this file carries the data.
